vision._note: gopiv is a BENCH TEST RIG (one motor, no wheels, never on the playfield); no physical AprilTag is mounted. robot_tag_id inherited from the template for schema completeness only.
vision._tag_id_note: 2026-08-27, stakeholder: this robot physically carries tag 54. Corrected from 100. The 100 in this file did not match the marker actually mounted on the robot -- a stale config value, not a renumbering. Anything that resolved gopiv by tag 100 (an aprilcam mobile-tag registration in particular) must be re-registered against 54, or it will report the wrong robot's centre.
vision._units_note: tag_offset_x/y/z are MILLIMETRES, the tag relative to the CENTRE OF ROTATION in the robot frame (x forward, y left). tag_offset_yaw is DEGREES and is the FULL mount yaw: -90 (AprilCam's fixed front-edge-to-hat convention, see pxt-nezha-diffdrive .claude/rules/tag-yaw-is-the-front-edge-not-the-hat.md) plus the physical plate residual. Feed it to the daemon as mount_yaw_rad; do NOT add the 90 again in your own code. Nothing read tag_offset_yaw as of 2026-09-05, so this fixes the convention: it matches tigez's previous non-schema tag_mount_yaw_deg -89.65, which was -90 + 0.35 residual.
vision._provenance: GOPIV-MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pxt-nezha-diffdrive tests/calibration/mount.py on the SECONDARY playfield (110x70, camera hd-usb-camera): 9 rest poses over 8 +-90 pivots, rms 15.9 mm, verification drift 0.66 cm/pivot -- POOR: the implied centre walked ~7 cm across the eight pivots (gopiv translates while it pivots), which breaks the single-centre assumption the solve rests on. Treat x/y as provisional and re-solve once the walking is understood. Heights are the stakeholder's tape measurements the same day. Artifact: reports/pf2-recal-20260905/19-mount-gopiv/mount.json. Residual +4.24 deg from a 300 mm probe.

geometry._geometry_note: 2026-08-27, camera-truthed on the main playfield, gopiv on firmware 0.20260827.2. trackwidth 114.8 mm is the STAKEHOLDER'S CALIPER measurement and is never corrected to make a turn land -- motion_engine.h is explicit that it is the one independently verifiable number in the geometry, and that all rotational scrub belongs in rotational_slip, since effectiveTrackWidth() = trackWidth / rotationalSlip. Was 128, which matched nothing. rotational_slip 0.9633 = 114.8 / 119.2, where 119.2 mm is the camera-measured EFFECTIVE track. METHOD, and why the first two attempts were wrong: effective track was derived from the SLOPE of a pivot sweep (4 sizes x 3 reps x both directions, 40/70/100/130 mm per wheel), fitting d_theta = 0.9616 deg/mm * d + 10.19 deg. Deriving it from any SINGLE pivot size instead gives a different answer every time -- 90 mm/wheel implied 107.4 mm and 47 mm/wheel implied 88.1 mm -- because a +10.2 deg FIXED per-pivot term (overshoot/coast, not scrub) is otherwise absorbed into the scale. That constant must NOT be folded into rotational_slip: slip is a scale, and baking the offset into it fits one pivot size and mis-turns every other. CLAUDE.md warns about exactly this shape -- a constant per-pivot offset does not cancel the way a scale error does. The 10.2 deg term is UNEXPLAINED and uncorrected; rotation_gain_*/rotation_offset_* below are where it would belong, but see the next note. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION: the pxt-nezha-diffdrive firmware carries its own baked defaults, motion_engine.h trackWidth_ = 114.2f and rotationalSlip_ = 0.952f, i.e. an effective track of 119.96 mm. The camera measurement here is 119.2 mm -- 0.6% apart, arrived at with no knowledge of those constants.
geometry._not_read_by_pxt_firmware_note: 2026-08-27: NOTHING in this geometry block reaches the pxt-nezha-diffdrive firmware. tools/make_deploy.py injects only the radio channel, kProfile, kVersion and the boot banner; test.ts never calls _setGeometry(); and grep finds no reader for rotation_gain_* or rotation_offset_* anywhere in that repo's src/. The robot runs motion_engine.h's baked trackWidth_/rotationalSlip_ instead. So editing this file changes host-side tooling and nothing on the robot. rotational_slip IS reachable at runtime -- it is a wire-settable config field (SET rotational_slip) -- but that is RAM-only and does not survive a reset. Changing what the robot ships with means editing motion_engine.h and reflashing.
geometry._tuning_note: MEASURED gopiv 2026-09-01 on the bench, pure odometry, pxt-nezha-diffdrive reports/gopiv-closure-20260901.md and captures/gopiv-profile-sweep-20260901/. Square-tour closure 75.6 mm untuned -> 10.8 mm +-1.5 over 5 tours, best single tour 2.2 mm, 17 tours under 10 mm. pivot_overrun cancels a CONSTANT +3.2 deg per-pivot over-rotation (measured at 15/45/90/180 deg; constant, not a scale). twist_hold_gain 8 cuts straight-leg heading drift 0.71 -> 0.18 deg; ABOVE 16 the heading servo goes unstable (24 gave +-30 deg oscillation). speed_floor 512 = 40 mm/s halves the final-tick heading quantum (1.6 -> 0.93 deg); 30 mm/s is NOT usable (stiction, sd 2.19 deg with 6-12 deg outliers). yaw_taper 800 halves pivot scatter again to sd 0.14 deg. All four are wire-settable (SET), not baked. Values obtained on a FRESH battery -- pivots degraded to +8.9 deg excess as the pack drained while straights stayed perfect, so re-tune or re-verify on a charged pack.

firmware_bake._provenance: GOPIV-MEASURED 2026-09-05 on the SECONDARY playfield (110x70, hd-usb-camera), over gopiv's own serial daemon on null. pxt-nezha-diffdrive reports/pf2-recal-20260905/21-turns-gopiv-lag*, 22-turns-gopiv-confirm. gopiv had NO firmware_bake at all and ran pure firmware defaults (confirmed live: lag 0.0, rotational_slip 0.952). lag_s 0.04 from the design's lag sweep -- lag moves the pivot OFFSET, not the gain: offset +12.96 deg at lag 0, +2.08 at 0.04, and mean abs error 5.98 -> 2.20 deg. (The lag 0.10 point is not comparable: one of its eight pivots terminated early at -46 deg, dragging its fit to gain 0.8589.) rotational_slip STAYS at the firmware default 0.952 and is pinned here explicitly because it is the value the sweep was measured against: the fit gain at lag 0.04 was 1.0009, i.e. already unity, so gopiv's effective track needs no correction (b_eff = 114.2/0.952 = 120.0 mm). travel_calib and trackwidth are deliberately NOT baked -- the distance run never completed (see below), so the only travel evidence is a single 300 mm probe that returned 300.9 mm.
firmware_bake._caveat: TWO UNRESOLVED FAULTS -- do not treat gopiv as calibrated. (1) EARLY-TERMINATED PIVOTS: 3 of 36 camera-scored pivots (8.3%) stopped part-way and still reported reason=stop -- -88.8 and +77.8 deg errors in the 12-pivot confirm, -46 deg in the lag 0.10 run. This was with --no-tlm, so it is NOT the known TLM-FULL-provokes-early-stops cause. Excluding them, the confirm run is 10/12 at mean abs 1.53 deg. (2) THE CENTRE OF ROTATION WANDERS: mean drift 1.2-1.5 cm per pivot against tigez's 0.35 and vevov's 0.39, the mount solve came out rms 15.9 mm with the implied centre walking 6.9 cm over eight pivots, and one large same-direction turn translated the robot 45 cm. Alternating +-90/180 sweeps hide this because their translations cancel, which is why the angle numbers above look clean. A mount solve and a rotational_slip both assume a fixed centre.

wheel_control._stall_note: 2026-08-09: added so this robot can be BUILT at all -- gen_boot_config.py requires all three (config-as-truth, sprint 114) and they were added to tovez.json only, which left gopiv and togov unbuildable. Held at 0, which is the documented INERT state, not a guess: tovez.json's own _stall_note says 'the whole detector is inert on any robot whose JSON leaves stall_window at 0'. gopiv has no drive characterization of its own, and tovez's numbers (15.0 / 40.0 / 500.0) are DESIGN CHOICES derived from tovez's own measured v_min, deadband and planner.a_max -- none of which have been measured here -- so borrowing them would be a fabricated calibration, not a default. Same posture togov.json takes for its uncharacterized wheel_control group. Replace with gopiv's own numbers before relying on stall detection on this robot. NOTE: togov.json still has this gap and is still unbuildable.
